text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- ABN Amro bank chairman Jan Kalff warns that businesses would suffer a blow, if EMU were to be postponed. (p1)
- Bank insurer ING Group is eyeing European markets for takeover candidates in run-up to Europe's single currency. (p1)
- Car company Renault's chairman Louis Schweitzer is to join Philips Electronics supervisory board. (p1)
- Tyre maker Vredestein's 1996 net grows 12 pct to 14.1 million guilders, helped by an early winter. (p3)
- Electronic firm De Drie Electronics posts 50,000 guilders higher 1996 net profit at 1.31 million guilders. (p3)
- Wild cat strike at carbon producer Norit highlights clash between works council and labour union. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Coalition parties abandon idea of a tax-cut from July, 1 due to less rosy outlook for public finances. (p1)
- Rabobank close to an agreement with U.S. Federal Reserve which had raised objections to its takeover of Dutch fund manager Robeco. (p2)
- Amsterdam's options exchange can hardly cope with the enormous volume of orders. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- EU ban on export of pigs prolonged by one week. (p1)
- Poll shows that more than half of Dutch people believe the Netherlands neds a second national airport or an expansion of existing Schiphol airport near amsterdam. (p6)
- Dutch economy set for an extra immpulse in 1998 as some two billion guilders are released from tax-exempt savings schemes started in 1994. (p7)
- Current chairman of Philips' supervisory board Floris Maljers will stay on for one more term. (p33)
TROUW
- Industrial group Stork's unit Fokker Aviation sets up aircraft maintenance centre in Singapore. (p7)
- Employees of Unilever's chemicals businesses, which Unilever plans to sell, are worried about their salaries and pensions. (p8)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) still dissatisfied with Dutch group Gist Brocades' penicillin production. (p11)
